Research workbench

Compare resolutions, track travelling waves and run parameter scans.

Choose a model or import a Studio configuration, then select Run study.

Study settings

Parameter sliders

Moving a slider replaces that parameter's formula with a number. Later dependent parameters are recalculated. Run to compute the changed model.

Full model JSON

Edit equations, initial data, lengths and boundary rows here, then apply. The numerical scope is the same as PDE Studio.

Spatial studies use N, 2N, 4N. Time studies use actual Δt, Δt/2, Δt/4. Parameter scans start every run from its specified initial data.

Solution

Contours, vector fields and surface angle

Vectors require a 2D plane and both expressions. Arrow lengths are normalized within each frame. Surface height shows the observation; its display mesh may be subsampled.

No trajectory

Run a study to inspect the trajectory.

Add a seed to periodic initial data

Add a Gaussian seed to the initial data, then rerun. This clears the selected field's reference formula.

Resolution comparison

Run three space or time levels to estimate an observed order.

Observables

Integrals use uniform-grid quadrature. Bounded probes in the half-cell boundary strip use the nearest cell-center value.

Parameter scan

Define the map metric

Wave maps use the field, reference, window and shift controls below. Balance maps use that same field index and require second-order bounded models. A threshold event is estimated from saved times; an event that was not seen is left missing.

Default: final RMS of u.

Click a cell to replay its trajectory. Red: failed run. Dash: unavailable data. Sensitivities use finite differences on the parameter grid.

Mass and heat balance

Recompute diffusive boundary input and other PDE terms from saved arrays. Available for second-order bounded models, including Robin.

Travelling-wave diagnostics

1D diagnostics. Phase alignment uses a fixed window and avoids extrapolating beyond bounded-domain samples.

Global, local and weighted curves: L² difference from the reference. Aligned shape: RMS on the selected window.
